description: We are a high school team from Astana, Kazakhstan, focused on the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. Our team brings together coding, engineering, and design skills to build an interactive web-based simulation. We are already fully formed and not looking for new members. Ready to build something amazing yeaaahh !!!!!
summary: Lunar Horizon is an interactive 3D web simulation and mission planning tool designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. When rocket launches are delayed due to Earth weather or hardware issues, mission planners must rapidly evaluate how date and location shifts affect landing feasibility. Our tool translates complex NASA topography and ephemeris data into an intuitive visual workspace. Users can simulate Earth-to-Moon trajectories, test custom launch velocities and weather conditions, inspect real-time Sun and Earth horizon angles on the Moon without atmosphere, and compare two landing scenarios side by side. Guided by our AI Mission Advisor UFO-chan, Lunar Horizon makes complex astrodynamics accessible to both engineers and students.
details:
What It Does and How It Works:

Lunar Horizon is a browser-based 3D lunar mission simulator that bridges the gap between raw NASA datasets and rapid mission planning. Users can configure Earth launch conditions (wind speed, weather, solar storms), adjust launch velocity and mid-course trajectory corrections, and watch the spacecraft travel from Earth to lunar orbit using adjustable Time Warp (1x to 10,000x). On the lunar surface, users can explore 12 curated sites (including Artemis III South Pole candidates and historical Apollo, Chang'e, and Chandrayaan sites) or click directly on an interactive elevation map to pick custom coordinates.

Key Features and Scientific Accuracy:

- Rapid Dual-Scenario Comparison: Users can run and compare two different Site + Date combinations simultaneously to evaluate how schedule delays affect solar illumination windows, Earth direct-to-Earth communication (accounting for Earth's libration), and landing safety.

- Real Physics & Astrodynamics Engine: All trajectories, fuel consumption, lunar gravity braking, and atmosphere-free horizon shadows are calculated dynamically in real time.

- Interactive AI Tutor (UFO-chan): Built-in conversational aerospace assistant explains orbital formulas and helps optimize mission parameters for users of all skill levels.

Tools, Source Code & Disclosure:

Built as a single-page web application using HTML5, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (WebGL), and procedural Web Audio API sound synthesis. Full source code is publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/gankonadoni95/Lunar-Horizon

Code structure, mathematical logic, and procedural audio synthesis were assisted by Claude AI. Our project logo and main mascot sprite (UFO-chan) were originally hand-drawn by our team member, while the sleeping title variant was generated with AI assistance.
